title: Adaptive batching and KV-cache warmup study for FP8/INT8 serving under mixed-length workloads
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: characterize end-to-end throughput and latency behavior for FP8 and INT8 quantized serving variants when exposed to realistic mixed-length request distributions, with focus on the interaction between adaptive batching, KV-cache warmup (prefix reuse), and long-context tail latency.

Problem: prior quantization benchmarks emphasized steady-state throughput on synthetic fixed-length workloads. In production we observe: (1) variable-length prompts (64->32k tokens) that change batching efficiency, (2) KV-cache warmup artifacts where initial requests that build cache suffer different quantization-induced accuracy drift, and (3) tail latency spikes for long-context requests under mixed-priority batches. We need a targeted study to inform routing policies, batching knobs, and calibration windows for progressive quant variants.

Scope: evaluate FP8 and INT8 variants across: (a) sequence length buckets [0-128,129-512,513-2048,2049-8192,8193+], (b) adaptive batching strategies (time-window, size-window, latency-priority), (c) KV-cache states (cold, warm-after-1, warm-after-8), and (d) mixed-tenant noise (10% high-priority low-latency requests). Produce recommendations for: default batch policy, minimum KV-cache warmup tokens before routing to INT8/FP8, and rollback SLO triggers for accuracy regressions.

Success criteria: actionable policy recommendations with measured trade-offs (throughput vs p95/p99 latency and accuracy delta relative to FP16 baseline).
acceptance_criteria: Bench harness produces reproducible results for each sequence length bucket and batching policy (seeded workloads)
Measured throughput and latency (median, p95, p99) for FP16, FP8, and INT8 variants across KV-cache states
Accuracy validation against eval prompt-set: delta in top-1 token perplexity and selected end-to-end eval prompts under each quant variant < 2% for acceptable lanes or clearly flagged otherwise
A short runbook with recommended default routing/batching knobs and warmup thresholds suitable for runtime-1.22
PR with harness code and dashboards (Grafana) linked and reviewed by RL/Applied ML

benchmark_results: H100 (1x): FP16 baseline - batch policy=static-size(16): throughput 1050 tokens/s, median latency 42ms (0-128), p95 110ms
H100 (1x): FP8 - batch policy=time-window(10ms): throughput 1950 tokens/s (1.86x), median latency 46ms, p95 132ms when cold cache
H100 (1x): INT8 - with per-layer activation rescale: throughput 2100 tokens/s (2.0x), median latency 48ms, p95 140ms; INT8 without rescale had large accuracy regressions
KV-cache effect: warm-after-8 reduces p95 by ~18-25ms across quant variants for buckets >2048 tokens; cold cache increases p99 by up to 40% for INT8

Mixed-tenant: injecting 10% small high-priority requests increases p99 of large-context lanes by 15-30ms under time-window batching; size-window batching reduces interference but lowers overall throughput by ~12%
decisions: Adopt progressive calibration snapshots for FP8 and INT8; require activation rescale pass for INT8 before enabling in production
Default runtime routing: use size-window batching for mixed-tenant clusters where >20% of requests are short (<128 tokens). Use time-window for latency-sensitive single-tenant Dedicated pools.
Set KV-cache warmup threshold to 512 tokens for routing to INT8 in long-context buckets; FP8 allowed after 128 tokens in most cases
Expose 'prefer-latency' flag to customers to opt out of aggressive batching which can degrade p99 for mixed workloads
